newsitem.title: KUWAIT: U.S. erects memorial for Gulf War dead in Kuwait.
newsitem.headline: U.S. erects memorial for Gulf War dead in Kuwait.

text.p: A memorial for Americans killed in the 1991 Gulf War was erected in Kuwait on Monday in a ceremony which was earlier postponed due to security concerns.

"Kuwait will remain free," U.S. Ambassador Ryan Crocker told a ceremony at the U.S. embassy where a pillar carrying the names of 385 U.S. military personnel killed in the 1990-91 Gulf crisis was erected.
In late October the U.S. embassy warned American citizens to exercise particular caution in light of reported threats against U.S. interests in Kuwait.
The memorial ceremony was postponed but Crocker told Reuters on Monday Kuwait is "considered a perfectly secure environment for today's event".

He said Americans should always be cautious but "should in no way indicate they can't live a normal life" in Kuwait which was freed in 1991 from a seven-month Iraqi occupation by a U.S.-led, multinational military coalition.
In the past year 24 Americans and two Indians were killed in two separate bomb attacks against U.S. military interests in neighbouring Saudi Arabia.
A U.S. embassy official in Kuwait told Reuters on Monday "If there was something specific at the time (of the October threat) it is no longer there."
Monday's event was attended by U.S. Air Force Secretary Sheila Widnall, senior U.S. military officers in charge of troops based in the Gulf Arab state and Kuwaiti representatives.

"This is a moment to reaffirm that the principles which underlay this sacrifice guide us today...Our commitment to the security and stability of Kuwait and the Gulf is unshakeable," Crocker told the ceremony.
"It is a commitment that we have backed up with U.S. military deployments in the face of Iraqi threats, most recently in September," he added.

Washington sent extra troops and military hardware to Kuwait in September in a standoff with Baghdad. There are more than 7,000 Americans in Kuwait, including 4,600 troops of the Kuwait Task Force and a number of air force personnel.
